title: Sharper | Securing America’s Defense Industrial Base
gist: CNAS 'Sharper' newsletter on the US defense industrial base: six months of war with Iran have depleted interceptor and precision munitions stockpiles below replacement rates; featured reports argue for 'affordable mass' to supplement exquisite munitions for a Taiwan contingency and criticize the Pentagon for prioritizing long-term development over near-term deterrence.

insights.claim: Six months of war with Iran have left US interceptor and precision weapon stockpiles dangerously low, with demand above the production replacement rate.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Sustained demand for missile/interceptor producers and capacity expansion funding.
insights.quote: leaving stockpiles of interceptors and precision weapons dangerously low and demand above the replacement rate of production
insights.locator: Six months of war with Iran

insights.claim: Becca Wasser argues the push for low-cost munitions is unlikely to materially affect the Iran war anytime soon.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Near-term relief must come from legacy primes, not new low-cost entrants.
insights.quote: “The push for low-cost munitions is unlikely to have a material effect on the Iran War—at least not anytime soon,”

insights.claim: Stacie Pettyjohn says low-cost interceptors are complements, not substitutes, for the PAC-3.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Low-cost interceptor startups add to rather than displace incumbent interceptor demand.
insights.quote: “They are complements, not substitutes, for the PAC-3,”

insights.claim: In a full-scale Taiwan invasion the US could need to strike more than 2,000 targets, so exquisite munitions must be replenished and supplemented with lower-cost weapons to reverse the inventory disadvantage.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Supports demand for both exquisite munitions and low-cost drone/missile makers.
insights.quote: a scenario in which the United States could be required to strike more than 2,000 targets
insights.locator: Although drones have been used extensively

insights.claim: Disproportionate investment in long-term developmental programs has left the Pentagon less able to meet near-term deterrence needs against China's accelerating buildup.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Possible reallocation toward procurement of existing systems over R&D programs.
insights.quote: Disproportionate investments in long-term developmental programs have left the Pentagon less able to meet the need for near-term deterrence.

insights.claim: The DIB is changing with new entrants and forms of financing, with venture capitalists and start-up executives among 14 contributors on reform.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Venture-backed defense entrants are a growing part of the base.
